texto: When the person who acts is not the one who performs the second action, «damit»: **Ich spreche langsam, damit du mich verstehst** should be used (I speak slowly for you to understand me). In German it is used indicative with the verb at the end, equivalent to the Spanish subjunctive.

If the subjects were the same, «um … zu» (**Ich lerne, um zu bestehen**) is preferred. But if another person intervenes, «damit» is the only alternative: **Ich helfe dir, damit du die Prüfung bestehst**.

frases.de: Warum sprichst du so langsam, Julia?
frases.en: Why are you talking so slow, Julia?

frases.de: Ich spreche langsam, damit du mich gut verstehst.
frases.es: Hablo despacio para que me entiendas bien.
frases.en: I talk slowly so you understand me well.
analisis: so you can understand me well

frases.de: Das ist sehr nett! Kannst du mir auch die Aufgabe erklären?
frases.es: ¡Eso es muy amable! ¿Puedes explicarme también el ejercicio?
frases.en: That's very kind! Can you explain the exercise to me too?

frases.de: Natürlich, ich erkläre es dir, damit wir fertig werden.
frases.es: Por supuesto, te lo explico para que terminemos.
frases.en: Of course, I'll explain it to you so we can finish.

bloques.pregunta: Why is «damit» required in «Ich spreche langsam, damit du mich verstehst»?

opciones.texto: Because subjects on both sides are different.
opciones.explicacion: «Ich» performs the first action and «du» performs the second.

opciones.texto: Because the verb of the subordinate is an infinitive
opciones.explicacion: «damit» goes with conjugated verb, not infinitive.

opciones.texto: Because it expresses cause and not purpose

bloques.pregunta: What position does the verb conjugate in a «damit» clause?

opciones.texto: At the absolute end of the subordinate
opciones.explicacion: As a subordinate conjunction, «damit» sends the conjugated verb at the end.
That would be the order of a main or coordinated prayer.

opciones.texto: In front of the subject of the subordinate
opciones.explicacion: The conjugated verb does not precede the subject in the subordinate.

bloques.frase: Ich spreche langsam, damit du mich ___ .

opciones.explicacion: A conjugated verb in 2nd person (du verstehst) placed at the end of the subordinate.

bloques.frase: Die Mutter gibt dem Sohn Geld, ___ er sich ein Buch kauft.

opciones.explicacion: With different subjects (die Mutter / er) «damit» is necessarily used.
«um» would demand «zu + infinitivo» and the same subject.

bloques.frase: Ich spreche langsam, damit du mich verstehst.

opciones.texto: I'm talking slow to make you understand me.
opciones.explicacion: spreche langsam = I speak slowly; damit = for that; verstehst = understand.

opciones.texto: I talk slowly because I don't understand you.
opciones.explicacion: Confusion «damit» with «weil» and reverse the meaning.

opciones.texto: You talk slowly so I understand you.

bloques.frase: Tim hilft seiner Schwester, damit sie die Prüfung ___ .

opciones.explicacion: Word conjugated in 3rd person singular (sie besteht) at the end of the subordinate with damit.

bloques.frase: Ich spreche langsam damit du mich verstehst
bloques.traduccion: I speak slowly so you understand me.
bloques.explicacion: damit introduces the final subordinate with verb at the end.

intro: The subordinating conjunction «damit» («so that») is used to express the purpose of an action, and is mandatory when the subjects of both clauses are **distintos**. The subordinate verb is conjugated and goes to the end.
